cases.title: Alaska Nurse Practitioner Gets 26 Years in 3 Overdose Deaths
cases.setting: Purported chronic pain and addiction clinic in Eagle River operated by an advanced nurse practitioner for over five years; District of Alaska
cases.drug: Opioids and other drugs, often prescribed in dangerous combinations
cases.method: Prescribed very large quantities of opioids and other drugs without legitimate medical purpose, with little to no medical justification, treatment plans, testing or physical examinations; ignored overdose history, pregnancy, taper requests, and warnings from family members, pharmacists, other providers and thousands of insurer warning letters
cases.status: Sentenced Nov. 12, 2026 to 26 years in prison after pleading guilty to causing three overdose deaths; an earlier jury conviction (five overdose deaths, 30-year sentence) was overturned because the presiding judge failed to recuse himself

cases.title: Three Detroit Doctors Indicted in Cash-Only Pill Mill Case
cases.setting: Woodward Boulevard Medical Building (WBMB), an alleged fraudulent "cash only" clinic in Detroit; doctors recruited and paid through CRW Worldwide, LLC and CRW Development, Inc.; Eastern District of Michigan
cases.method: Alleged: "patients" paid $250-$500 cash per visit for requested opioid prescriptions; new patients were screened by asking "who sent you"; recruiters paid office fees and pharmacy copays and sold the pills on the street market
cases.status: Indictment unsealed Oct. 22, 2026 against Dr. Luis Rodriguez, Dr. Nayantara Jnananand, Dr. Prashanti Franklin, Clara Wilkerson and Latanya Wallace-Hardiman on drug conspiracy and related charges; Wilkerson and Wallace-Hardiman also charged with money laundering; maximum 20 years per count; an indictment is only a charge

cases.title: Patient Recruiter Pleads Guilty in Florida Oxycodone Scheme
cases.setting: Patient recruiter working with South Florida clinics and doctors and with pharmacies of Olushola Yusuf, a pharmacist and pharmacy owner convicted at trial earlier in 2026; Southern District of Florida
cases.drug: Oxycodone 30mg (conspiracy involving over 87,000 pills; Llerena personally responsible for 3,735)
cases.method: Paid recruits to pose as patients and obtain unnecessary oxycodone prescriptions, brought them to Yusuf's pharmacies, which kept a list of his recruits, paid Yusuf cash above market value, paid recruits via Zelle and resold the pills on the street
cases.status: Pleaded guilty to conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance; maximum penalty 20 years in prison; no date for the penalty hearing stated in the release

cases.title: CVS Agrees to Pay $315M Over Unlawfully Filled Opioid Prescriptions and False Claims
cases.setting: CVS Pharmacy Inc. and related corporate entities, pharmacy chain based in Rhode Island; complaint filed Dec. 13, 2024 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island
cases.drug: Opioids and other controlled substances, including "trinity" prescriptions (an opioid, a benzodiazepine and a muscle relaxant)
cases.method: Alleged: filled prescriptions that lacked a legitimate medical purpose or were not issued in the usual course of professional practice (dangerous and excessive opioid quantities, early fills, pill-mill prescribers) despite red flags, then billed many to federal healthcare programs
cases.status: Civil settlement announced Oct. 13, 2026: $315 million, plus a memorandum of agreement with DEA requiring a reporting hotline for employees and the public, proactive monitoring of pharmacy dispensing patterns, and a process to evaluate suspected prescribers. Whistleblower Hillary Estright's share not yet determined (U.S. ex rel. Estright v. CVS Health Corp., No. 22-cv-00222, D.R.I.)

cases.title: Doctor Convicted of Distributing Over 2 Million Stimulant Pills on the Done ADHD Platform

cases.drug: Adderall and other stimulants, including methamphetamine and amphetamines (over 2 million pills)
cases.method: Prescribed stimulants to paying subscribers without examining them, including a patient with an active substance use disorder and a patient he knew had a schizophrenia diagnosis, and continued after warnings; recruited other medical professionals to the scheme and earned referral bonuses
cases.status: Convicted by a federal jury Oct. 2, 2026 of one count of conspiracy to distribute controlled substances and six counts of distribution of controlled substances; maximum penalty 140 years; sentencing date not set

cases.title: Telehealth Firm Done Global Indicted in $100M Adderall Distribution Scheme

cases.drug: Adderall and other stimulants — over 40 million pills prescribed
cases.method: Structured telehealth platform to push stimulant prescriptions regardless of medical need — limited prescriber information, mandated sub-30-minute visits, auto-refill subscriptions, paid prescribers only per prescription written
cases.status: He and Brody arrested Jun 13, 2024 on health care fraud and drug distribution conspiracy charges; both later convicted at trial

cases.title: Hospital Pharmacy Manager Stole 35,000+ Opioid Vials from Secure Vault
cases.setting: Pharmacy manager, IU Health Ball Memorial Hospital (Muncie, IN)
cases.drug: Hydromorphone (~317,000 mg) + methadone (~41,390 mg) + morphine (290 mg) — 35,000+ vials
cases.method: Diverted an average of ~500 vials/month from the secure vault over ~5 years; hospital audit and search warrant found drugs at his home. Diversion was allegedly disguised using normally-unused transaction types recorded as legitimate transfers to the hospital's outpatient clinics. Also reported: Charge as worded in the source: Level 3 felony possession of narcotic drugs over 28 grams; Level 5 felony theft over $50,000; Level 6 felonies for fraud, forgery and unlawful possession of syringes.
cases.status: Arrested Jul 2024; felony charges filed Aug 2025 — possession, theft, obtaining a controlled substance by fraud/deceit, unlawful possession of a syringe, forgery; case pending
