cases.title: Physician at Green Mountain Family Medicine diverted controlled substances by writing staff members' prescriptions for personal and family use
cases.location: Rutland and White River Junction, VT
cases.drug: Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen (Schedule II), Lorazepam (Schedule IV), Diazepam (Schedule IV), Tramadol (Schedule IV), Carisoprodol (Schedule IV)
cases.method: The physician admitted to writing and receiving at least nine controlled-substance prescriptions in staff members' names for his own use from May 2013 through October 2015, writing at least four such prescriptions in staff members' names for an immediate family member's use, and altering staff medical records to include false information about the prescriptions.
cases.status: The Board reprimanded the physician; suspended his Vermont medical license for five years with time served from June 21, 2016; permanently prohibited him from prescribing Schedule II-V controlled substances in Vermont; required practice monitoring, treatment, and a $9,000 administrative penalty.

cases.title: Registered nurse alleged to have diverted controlled substances from a rehabilitation facility in Burlington
cases.method: Alleged to have diverted controlled substances from the facility on or around December 3, 2019.
cases.status: License surrender accepted; final decision and order dated September 10, 2020; no petition for reinstatement for at least one year and $632 costs before any application is considered.

cases.title: Assisted living facility nurse diverted Vicodin from a resident for personal use
cases.method: Diverted Vicodin from a resident for personal use on April 30 and May 1, 2019.
cases.status: License suspended for an indefinite period; suspension may be stayed upon compliance with conditions including treatment, monitoring, and practice limitations.

cases.title: Registered nurse accused of diverting controlled substances from Wisconsin health care facilities
cases.setting: multiple health care facilities in Wisconsin
cases.method: Alleged diversion of controlled substances from facilities for personal use and repeated improper administration and wasting of controlled substances; complaints also alleged obtaining and ingesting steroids without a prescription, stealing saline syringes, impairment at work, and failed reasonable suspicion drug tests.
cases.status: Interim order suspending the registered nurse license pending final resolution; the nurse voluntarily agreed not to practice in Wisconsin or under multistate privileges during the investigation.

cases.title: Skilled nursing facility registered nurse diverted Ativan tablets from PRN supply for personal use; Vermont license warned
cases.setting: Foulkeways at Gwynedd Skilled Nursing Facility
cases.method: Admitted to diverting Ativan tablets for personal use in 2015 or 2016 on more than one occasion by taking them from the PRN supply at the skilled nursing facility; the Board found this constituted diverting drugs for unauthorized use and failing to exercise independent professional judgment.
cases.status: License warned; no other conditions or sanctions imposed. Board found Violations Two and Four proven; Violations One and Three not proven.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician diverted a customer's oxycodone prescription at a Hagerstown pharmacy
cases.method: Alleged diversion of a customer's prescription: the technician was given the prescription, carried it with two others to the front register but gave only one to the cashier, placed the oxycodone prescription back in the customer waiting area, later removed the pills from the bag and put them in her pocket, and deleted the prescription on hold. She admitted to the pharmacy's asset protection manager that she diverted the oxycodone pills to self-medicate a back injury, and admitted in a written statement that she took a patient's medication and emptied 45 pills into her pocket.
cases.status: Registration to practice as a pharmacy technician revoked by final order; the Board found diversion of a controlled dangerous substance.

cases.title: CVS pharmacy manager diverted hydromorphone tablets and liquid solution for personal use; license revoked
cases.setting: a CVS Pharmacy in Berlin, Vermont
cases.drug: hydromorphone 8 mg tablets and liquid hydromorphone 1 mg/mL solution
cases.method: Diverted controlled substances from the pharmacy for personal use from about March 2021 to September 2021; admitted diverting approximately 100 hydromorphone 8 mg tablets from a 100-count bottle over several months and an unknown amount of liquid hydromorphone 1 mg/mL solution. Documented the expected tablet count as in stock knowing the count was off because of the diversion, ordered liquid hydromorphone with no legitimate reason, and told investigators he replaced the diverted liquid volume with distilled water to make the bottle appear full; testing revealed diphenhydramine in the solution.
cases.status: License revoked; the Board of Pharmacy found the pharmacist in default and treated the Specification of Charges as proven

cases.title: Pharmacist-in-charge diverted hydrocodone and tramadol powder from a pharmacy controlled-substance safe; Maryland license revoked
cases.setting: a pharmacy in Virginia (name omitted from the order)
cases.drug: Hydrocodone powder (schedule II) and Tramadol powder (schedule IV)
cases.method: Alleged theft of a controlled substance from the pharmacy; a pharmacy video camera captured the pharmacist-in-charge removing medication from the controlled substance safe and placing it in his pocket or into a cup; an inventory found 847 mg of tramadol powder and 2,947 mg of hydrocodone powder missing; the pharmacy president stated the pharmacist admitted taking controlled substances, including hydrocodone powder, and using them in his coffee and other beverages while working; the pharmacist admitted to Virginia Board investigators that he diverted controlled substances from the pharmacy for personal use between August 13, 2021 and October 13, 2021.
cases.status: Maryland pharmacist license revoked; order reportable to the National Practitioner Data Bank

cases.title: Registered nurse diverted and consumed Oxycodone on-shift in cardiac surgery unit
cases.method: diverted and consumed Oxycodone while working on-shift; disclosed to the Board
cases.status: voluntarily surrendered registered nurse license

cases.title: Agency nurse accused of diverting fentanyl at Watertown hospital; interim suspension
cases.setting: a hospital located in Watertown, Wisconsin
cases.method: Alleged diversion and use of fentanyl while working as an agency nurse assigned to a hospital located in Watertown, Wisconsin; the Board had not determined whether any statutes or rules were violated.
cases.status: Interim order accepted; privilege to practice as a registered nurse in Wisconsin under the Nurse Licensure Compact suspended during the pendency of the disciplinary matter, effective 10/12/2023.

cases.title: Registered nurse charged with stealing oxycodone and hydrocodone/acetaminophen from residents at Prince George Healthcare Center
cases.method: Allegedly stole for personal use and withheld a quantity of oxycodone and hydrocodone/acetaminophen prescribed to six residents while working as a registered nurse.
cases.status: Arrested and booked on six counts of exploitation of a vulnerable adult and six counts of theft of a controlled substance, first offense.

cases.title: Pharmacist-in-charge convicted of conspiring to dispense oxycodone through a co-owned pharmacy to individuals with illegitimate prescriptions
cases.setting: a pharmacy co-owned and operated by the pharmacist-in-charge
cases.method: pleaded guilty to conspiracy to distribute and dispense a controlled substance; admitted that through a pharmacy he co-owned and operated as pharmacist-in-charge, he and co-conspirators dispensed oxycodone 30 mg pills to individuals with obviously illegitimate prescriptions for cash.
cases.status: Maryland pharmacy license revoked; sentenced to 78 months' imprisonment followed by three years' supervised release.

cases.title: Registered nurse removed propofol from workplace for personal use
cases.method: removed narcotic medication from her place of employment for personal use; pharmacy audit records showed multiple bottles of propofol were prematurely replaced; documentation audit showed several unaccounted propofol bottles; acknowledged removing medication from the facility for personal use to address sleeping issues
cases.status: Stipulated Order for Probation; license placed on probation; prohibited from access to narcotics or controlled substances without written approval

cases.title: Pharmacy technician diverted controlled substance from pharmacy (agreed board order)
cases.method: diversion
cases.status: Voluntary revocation

cases.title: Pharmacy technician diverted controlled substance from pharmacy (default board order)
cases.method: diversion
cases.status: Revocation

cases.title: Pharmacy technician took controlled substances from pharmacy (default board order)
cases.method: took
cases.status: Revocation

cases.title: Registered nurse diverted and abused controlled substances from places of employment
cases.method: diverted controlled substances from places of employment and abused those controlled substances; failed to answer truthfully about drug diversion and substance abuse during license renewal and a Board investigation; medication documentation discrepancies including delays, wasting full packages instead of returning them, failing to document administrations, logging out medications hours early, unaccounted medications, and documenting administration before logging out
cases.status: Suspension with conditions followed by probation; licensee admitted the allegations

cases.title: Registered nurse accused of obtaining controlled substance by fraud from resident's supply at North Hills Lifecare and Rehab
cases.method: Allegedly signed out two tablets of a controlled substance from a resident's prescription supply after the resident had been discharged and transferred to another unit; documentation indicated the medication was administered, but the resident did not receive it, and the tablets were later found missing from inventory.
cases.status: Arrested on one count of Obtaining Drugs by Fraud, a Class D felony.

cases.title: Registered nurse stole fentanyl vials at work and altered medication logs to conceal theft
cases.method: Stole 255 vials of fentanyl 100 mcg/2 mL and altered medication logs attempting to conceal the theft; tested positive for fentanyl on a for-cause drug screen at work; pleaded guilty and was convicted in federal court of felony acquiring or obtaining possession of a controlled substance by misrepresentation, fraud, forgery, deception or subterfuge.
cases.status: License placed on 36-month probation; terms include no access to narcotics or controlled substances; Board order.

cases.title: Hospital lead pharmacy technician diverted Oxycodone by substituting Fludrocortisone during prepackaging for automated dispensing system
cases.setting: a hospital in Prince George's County, Maryland
cases.method: Switched Oxycodone 5 mg tablets with Fludrocortisone 0.1 mg tablets during prepackaging to refill an automated medication dispensing system and entered zero-count refills to conceal the swap; admitted to personally ingesting the Oxycodone.
cases.status: Registration revoked.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician diverted alprazolam, zolpidem and other controlled substances from a national pharmacy chain in Easton, Maryland, by taking pills from bottles
cases.setting: a national pharmacy chain, at two stores in Easton, Maryland
cases.drug: Alprazolam (Xanax), zolpidem (Ambien), carisoprodol (Soma), diazepam, eszopiclone (Lunesta), and clonazepam
cases.method: Stole controlled substances from the pharmacy's stores by taking them from pill bottles; was seen consuming alprazolam tablets and placing additional tablets in a lab coat pocket; admitted stealing multiple controlled substances.
cases.status: Final order of revocation of pharmacy technician registration; registration revoked.

cases.title: Unlicensed Director of Nursing at Cherrydale Post Acute charged with stealing oxycodone from a person
cases.method: Allegedly stole a quantity of oxycodone, a Schedule II controlled substance, from another person with intent to permanently deprive that person of the medication while employed at Cherrydale Post Acute.
cases.status: Arrested and charged with one count of Theft of a Controlled Substance, first offense, and two counts of Unlicensed Practice as Registered Nurse or Practical Nurse; booked into the Greenville County Detention Center. Presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

cases.title: ER charge nurse self-reported diverting medication wastes for personal use at Ascension St. Vincent Anderson
cases.method: self-reported diverting medication wastes for personal use; terminated for violating the drug policy
cases.status: self-reported to PLA; terminated; enrolled in IPRP in August 2025 and signed a 3-year RMA; board recommended renewal on probation for the length of the RMA, with CEUs and referral of pending criminal charges to the OAG

cases.title: Nurse charged with obtaining a controlled substance by fraud or deceit and wasting narcotics at Community North
cases.method: charged with obtaining a controlled substance by fraud or deceit; diversion was suspended due to wasting of narcotics at work; positive drug test for marijuana
cases.status: entered a diversion program that was completed and charges dismissed and expunged in October 2025; self-reported to ISNAP and entered a monitoring agreement; board recommended renewal free and clear

cases.title: Hospital nurse found with Dilaudid and Hydrocodone waste in pocket from work
cases.method: charged with possession of a narcotic drug and public intoxication; pled guilty to possession of a narcotic drug; had waste in pocket from work consisting of a Dilaudid pill and a Hydrocodone pill; terminated from Methodist Hospital
cases.status: pled guilty in January 2025; completed probation in January 2026; terminated in August 2024; was unsuccessfully discharged from ISNAP in July 2025; board recommended renewal on indefinite probation, reengagement with ISNAP, a 3- to 5-year RMA, and CEUs

cases.title: Rehabilitation center nurse accused of stealing patients' painkillers and drug logs
cases.setting: a rehabilitation center in Sandy, Utah
cases.method: Alleged to have stolen medications and drug logs from patients at the rehabilitation center where the nurse worked; police stated the nurse admitted to taking medications over the previous two months, allegedly taking drugs from patients who had multiple packs knowing they would not notice they were missing.
cases.status: Arrested and booked into the Salt Lake County Jail; charged with one felony count of pattern of unlawful activity and several misdemeanors including theft and intentional abuse or neglect of a vulnerable adult.

cases.title: Registered nurse removed fentanyl from medication safe without order or documentation and failed to document controlled substance administration/wasting; license revoked
cases.setting: Grants Pass Surgery Center, Hearthstone Nursing and Rehabilitation Center, Bay Area Hospital
cases.drug: fentanyl, oxycodone, hydromorphone, alprazolam, lorazepam, tramadol
cases.method: removed fentanyl from a medication safe without a written order or documentation; failed to document administration or wasting of controlled substances; wasted oxycodone without allowing a witness to verify the medication; delayed wasting of controlled substances
cases.status: Registered nurse license revoked

cases.title: Hospital nurse accused of stealing opioids from patients at Grand Strand Medical Center
cases.method: Allegedly stole opioid drugs on six separate occasions while working at the hospital, under the guise of providing them to patients, and then either failed to document taking them or fraudulently documented them as administered to a patient.
cases.status: Arrested on several charges of theft of controlled substances and violating drug distribution law; released after posting $12,000 bail.

cases.title: Licensed practical nurse charged with stealing oxycodone from resident at Simpsonville Post Acute
cases.method: Allegedly knowingly and intentionally took a quantity of Oxycodone belonging to a resident and diverted Oxycodone prescribed to the resident for personal use.
cases.status: Arrested and charged with one count of Theft of a Controlled Substance, 1st Offense; booked into Greenville County Detention Center; prosecution by the South Carolina Attorney General's Office.

cases.title: Registered nurse admitted obtaining and consuming oxycodone without a prescription and had controlled-substance administration and documentation errors involving two patients; voluntarily surrendered license
cases.method: Admitted obtaining and consuming oxycodone without a prescription; employer reported controlled-substance administration and documentation errors for two patients, and the licensee could not account for what medications were administered or why documentation was made; also admitted administering medication to a patient without a provider order and later admitted obtaining and consuming two oxycodone pills.
cases.status: Voluntary surrender of registered nurse license accepted; may apply for reinstatement after a minimum of three years.

cases.title: Registered nurse obtained Vyvanse from workplace without authorization and self-administered
cases.setting: Their workplace (as stated in the source)
cases.method: obtained a generic equivalent to Vyvanse from their workplace without a medical order and without authorization; took it home and administered it to themselves
cases.status: registered nurse license placed on 36-month probation; admitted allegations

cases.title: Registered nurse alleged to have obtained controlled substances from a Texas pharmacy using unauthorized prescriptions and co-worker prescriber numbers
cases.drug: Zolpidem Tartrate, Eszopiclone, Acetaminophen-Codeine #3, Guaifenesin-Codeine, Butalbital-Acetaminophen-Caffeine, and Hydrocodone
cases.method: Alleged to have obtained these medications from a pharmacy in Texas, for themself and a family member, through the use of unauthorized electronically communicated prescriptions, using the names and Drug Enforcement Administration numbers of three co-worker prescribers.
cases.status: Stipulated Order for Probation; license placed on probation, with a 24-month period of probation to begin upon return to supervised nursing practice. Any monitored practice completed in Texas in compliance with the Texas Board of Nursing order counts toward the 24 months.

cases.title: Licensed practical nurse found to have ingested prescription medications and possessed Adavan at Delaware Hospital for the Chronically Ill
cases.setting: Delaware Hospital for the Chronically Ill
cases.method: ingested several prescription medications without telling her supervisor; was found with Adavan in her pocket that should have been administered to a patient but was claimed missing; Hearing Officer found a pattern of theft and consumption of controlled substances
cases.status: Board suspended the license for five years, required monthly random drug screens, and required 12 CEs (6 in ethics, 6 in substance abuse)

cases.title: Sweetbriar Assisted Living nurse sentenced for hydrocodone theft and falsifying records
cases.method: obtaining hydrocodone by fraud; admitted stealing hydrocodone intended for patients for personal use and falsifying records to cover up the theft
cases.status: sentenced to five years of probation; previously pleaded guilty

cases.title: Former Trinity Home Health/Hospice nurses accused of diluting and diverting patients' morphine and hydromorphone
cases.drug: morphine and hydromorphone; prescription pain medication
cases.method: Allegedly diluted nursing home patients' medications; administered morphine instead of hydromorphone; brought unused medication back to the office after a patient died and ingested it; investigation found multiple instances of drug diversion.
cases.status: Charges across suspects include Endangering a Vulnerable Adult (B felony), Conspiracy (C felony), and Theft of Property (C felony); two former nurses voluntarily surrendered their nursing licenses after admitting to the drug-diversion allegations; arrest warrants were issued.

cases.title: Hospital nurse diverted hydrocodone intended for a patient and falsified records
cases.method: Admitted to taking two 5 mg hydrocodone pills intended for a patient, keeping them for personal use, and falsely documenting in the patient file that the medication had been given to the patient.
cases.status: Pleaded guilty to obtaining a controlled substance by misrepresentation, fraud, forgery, deception, and subterfuge; terminated from employment on June 27, 2015; faces up to four years in federal prison; sentencing set for October 1, 2018.

cases.title: Nevada nursing board found a licensed practical nurse withdrew morphine from patient dispensers at a rural hospital without documenting it
cases.setting: a rural hospital and nursing home in Caliente, Nevada
cases.method: withdrew morphine from the medication dispensers of two patients without documenting what happened to the controlled substance
cases.status: license stripped; barred from reapplying for five years

cases.title: Emergency room nurse suspended indefinitely for diverting controlled substances from an automated medication administration machine
cases.method: repeatedly withdrew controlled substances from an automated medication administration machine and failed to document that they were administered to patients; a drug screen showed three controlled substances in the nurse's system
cases.status: suspended until able to demonstrate twelve months of continued sobriety and thereafter placed on probation; the Georgia Board of Nursing's proposed sanction was upheld

cases.title: Registered nurse reprimanded for misappropriating narcotics from employer for personal use
cases.method: intentional misappropriation of various narcotics from employer for personal use
cases.status: Consent Agreement; public reprimand

cases.title: Three former Trinity Hospital hospice nurses accused of stealing drugs and endangering patients
cases.setting: Trinity Hospital's Home Health and Hospice program
cases.drug: morphine and hydromorphine; drugs prescribed for hospice patients
cases.method: Accused of stealing drugs prescribed for hospice patients; two charged with endangering a patient by diluting medication or giving morphine instead of prescribed hydromorphine; alleged conspiracy to steal drugs; one allegedly confessed to ingesting unused medication and self-administering for over a year; investigation found multiple drug diversions in records of 104 patients.
cases.status: Charged with felony offenses; two voluntarily surrendered nursing licenses after admitting to board allegations; one arrested and signed promise to appear.

cases.title: Health system settles alleged opioid diversion case over tens of thousands of missing oxycodone 30 mg tablets
cases.method: Alleged large-scale diversion of opioids; tens of thousands of oxycodone 30 mg tablets were reported missing over more than four years, and the health system allegedly failed to notify authorities of the suspected diversion within the time required by federal law.
cases.status: Agreed to pay $4.1 million to settle the claims; the system said it has since overhauled pharmacy recordkeeping and reporting and implemented electronic inventory systems. At the time, the largest settlement of its kind for hospital drug diversion; the DEA investigation was launched in 2017.

cases.title: Georgia hospital settles allegations over unaccounted 30 mg oxycodone tablets believed diverted
cases.method: allegedly failed to provide effective controls and procedures to guard against theft and loss of controlled substances, resulting in tens of thousands of 30 mg oxycodone tablets unaccounted for and believed diverted for illegal uses over a four-year period, and allegedly failed to notify DEA of suspected diversion within the requisite time period
cases.status: $4.1 million civil settlement and performance improvement plan with DEA

cases.title: Hospital pharmacy technician diverted hydrocodone and oxycodone from a pharmacy vault through fraudulent automated dispensing transactions
cases.drug: hydrocodone and oxycodone (Schedule II controlled substances)
cases.method: Stole 8,505 pills, each containing 5 milligrams of either hydrocodone or oxycodone, from the hospital's pharmacy vault between February 2017 and March 2018, using her authorized fingerprint and unique login to conduct 82 fraudulent transactions in the hospital's new automated medication distribution and tracking system, which she found did not require a valid prescription to dispense medication to patients being discharged; gave the pills to her boyfriend for his personal use and used some herself.
cases.status: Sentenced to 12 months in jail plus six years of court supervision; pleaded guilty in June to one count each of possessing with intent to distribute hydrocodone and oxycodone; had repaid $1,033 to the hospital before sentencing.

cases.title: Hilo clinic physician and employees accused of unlawfully distributing opioids
cases.method: accused of prescribing and unlawfully distributing powerful narcotics, sedatives and opioids such as hydrocodone, oxycodone, fentanyl and morphine
cases.status: arrested; scheduled to stand trial in U.S. District Court in June

cases.title: Las Vegas nurse sentenced for illegally prescribing hydrocodone and oxycodone in a cash-for-prescriptions scheme
cases.method: Alleged and admitted conduct: arranged with a surgical technician and a physician to give hydrocodone and oxycodone to patients without a legitimate medical purpose in exchange for cash, and wrote illegal prescriptions without a medical purpose; also billed Medicare and Medicaid for prescriptions for lidocaine, modafinil and diclofenac sodium without having examined the patient.
cases.status: Pleaded guilty to eight counts of distribution of a controlled substance and eight counts of health care fraud; sentenced to more than six years in federal prison, three years of supervised release, and ordered to pay $3,749,121 in restitution.

cases.title: Pharmacist stole Schedule IV controlled substances from Institutional Care Pharmacy
cases.drug: zolpidem, modafinil, clonazepam, tramadol, lorazepam, alprazolam
cases.method: stole controlled substances from employer; observed on security camera; admitted stealing; retrieved stolen drugs from purse and residence
cases.status: license suspended indefinitely; summary suspension removed

cases.title: Rawlins physician sentenced federally for dispensing medically unnecessary controlled substances
cases.drug: oxycodone, alprazolam, hydrocodone, tramadol and other controlled substances
cases.method: Pleaded guilty to 20 counts of dispensing medically unnecessary controlled substances; prosecutors said some patients were addicts or became addicted, that drugs were traded for sexual favors, and that 430 oxycodone pills were prescribed to a young female patient in return for lewd photographs.
cases.status: Sentenced to 20 concurrent five-year prison terms, six years of supervised release, a $2,000 special assessment and $400 restitution; license previously suspended by the state medical board.

cases.title: Nursing home licensed practical nurse convicted of diverting 638 narcotics pills from residents
cases.setting: Georgiana Health and Rehabilitation. Also referred to as Butler County Nursing Home in the Attorney General's release title.
cases.method: Diverted 638 narcotics pills, including hydrocodone, oxycodone, tramadol and lorazepam, from nursing home residents for whom the medications were intended; thefts occurred between November 5, 2020, and January 19, 2021.
cases.status: Pleaded guilty to four counts of second-degree theft of property; sentencing set for July 7; faces one to 10 years imprisonment and up to a $15,000 fine for each conviction.

cases.title: Emergency room nurse sentenced to probation for diverting fentanyl from a Lincoln hospital pharmacy
cases.method: Checked out fentanyl from the hospital pharmacy more than 200 times between May and June 2022; 55 discrepancies were found; 2.65 mg of fentanyl was unaccounted for; in some cases checked out fentanyl without a doctor's order and in others reported administering it within five minutes of patient discharge; denied stealing or using the drug but urine tested positive for fentanyl.
cases.status: Pleaded guilty to acquiring a controlled substance by fraud; sentenced to three years of probation; gave up nursing license.

cases.title: Surgical practice nurse sentenced for tampering with fentanyl, morphine, and meperidine and replacing them with saline
cases.method: extracted medication from vials of fentanyl, morphine, and meperidine and replaced it with saline, compromising at least 78 vials, including those intended for surgical patients; testing found compromised vials contained less than 15% of the actual medication and that tampering rendered multiple vials unsterile
cases.status: sentenced to 48 months in prison and three years of supervised release; pleaded guilty to the charges; plea agreement requires permanent surrender of the nursing license

cases.title: Registered nurse convicted of tampering with fentanyl citrate vials and obtaining controlled substance by fraud at Chamberlain hospital
cases.setting: a hospital in Chamberlain, South Dakota
cases.method: Tampered with a vial of fentanyl citrate for injection by removing the fentanyl and replacing the majority of it with saline solution, then returned the tampered vial to storage knowing the diluted fentanyl could be dispensed to surgical patients; also obtaining a controlled substance by misrepresentation, fraud, forgery, deception, and subterfuge.
cases.status: Convicted and sentenced to two years of probation and a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund.

cases.title: ICU nurse sentenced for tampering with fentanyl and hydromorphone at Ardmore hospital
cases.setting: Mercy Hospital Intensive Care Unit, Ardmore, Oklahoma
cases.method: stole fentanyl and hydromorphone intended for intensive care patients; removed the pain medication from vials, refilled the empty vials with tap water, and returned the tampered vials to the controlled storage locker; admitted the conduct
cases.status: sentenced to 12 months in prison for one count of Tampering with Consumer Products; pleaded guilty on August 31, 2023

cases.title: WakeMed nurse charged with stealing fentanyl from IV bag
cases.method: Allegedly had access to the drug through the job and stole 2,500 mL of fentanyl from an IV bag on Oct. 19.
cases.status: Charged with two felony counts: embezzling/diverting a controlled substance by registrant/employee and obtaining possession of a controlled substance by fraud/forgery; arrested Oct. 30; out on bond; next court date Nov. 19; no longer employed by WakeMed.

cases.title: Birmingham-area nursing home nurse diverted hydrocodone tablets; pleaded guilty to theft
cases.method: The nurse, responsible for distributing medication to residents, stole opioid tablets from the nursing home. A nurse discovered missing hydrocodone in July 2024, and an investigation found discrepancies involving over 100 hydrocodone tablets over approximately two months. The nurse was terminated by the facility after the missing hydrocodone was discovered.
cases.status: Pled guilty to Theft of Property in the Second Degree, a Class C felony; received a 15-month suspended sentence.

cases.title: Hospital pharmacist diverted ketamine and falsified destruction records at Mercy Hospital Anderson Pharmacy
cases.drug: ketamine, a Schedule III controlled substance
cases.method: The Board found the pharmacist stole ketamine from his employer pharmacy over about six months, sold two bottles for $100 each, provided ketamine to a drug dealer, and falsified drug destruction records by showing a vial to a witness, having the required form signed, then leaving without destroying the drugs.
cases.status: Permanently revoked the pharmacist license; removed the summary suspension order.

cases.title: Muncie hospital pharmacy license put on probation after pharmacy manager diverted opioids using unused transaction types
cases.method: The attorney general's administrative complaint alleged the hospital failed over a 44-month period to maintain effective controls against theft and diversion of controlled substances, allowing a pharmacy manager to repeatedly remove Schedule II narcotics through normally-unused transaction types while disguising the withdrawals as legitimate transfers to two outpatient clinics. Investigators said the reported losses included more than 32,000 milliliters of hydromorphone, more than 3,300 milliliters of methadone solution, more than 4,000 methadone tablets and smaller amounts of morphine, with the hospital estimating its loss at more than $121,000.
cases.status: The Indiana Board of Pharmacy voted 3-2 to accept a revised settlement placing the hospital's pharmacy license and controlled substance registration on indefinite probation for at least three years, imposing the maximum $44,000 civil fine plus a $5 statutory fee, and requiring quarterly independent audits, two unannounced compliance inspections, a drug diversion certificate program for pharmacy leadership and additional diversion-prevention continuing education. Also reported: The hospital's pharmacy license and controlled substances registration were placed on indefinite probation for not less than three years, with quarterly outside audits for the first two years, two unannounced compliance inspections, required diversion-prevention training for pharmacy leadership, and a $44,000 fine; the hospital reported the loss to the DEA and Board in July 2024 and filed an amended DEA Form 106 in November 2024, and in August 2025 the county prosecutor's office filed charges against the pharmacist.

cases.title: Registered nurse accused of diverting morphine from OrthoNebraska surgical unit
cases.method: Alleged entering fictitious orders in patient charts to divert morphine for himself; admitted diverting morphine by adding or changing the ordered amount, charting the difference, or charting medical 'waste'; accessed automated medication dispensing machine, sometimes using co-workers' login information.
cases.status: Booked on seven felony counts of intentionally violating a narcotic drug law; placed on leave then later fired; scheduled court appearance. Nebraska nursing license was listed as active until Oct. 31, 2026, as of the report, with no disciplinary information shown.

cases.title: Edmond hospital employee charged with stealing fentanyl waste from OU Health
cases.method: Accused of diverting fentanyl waste: a hospital report flagged more than 15 transactions involving fentanyl waste, including 'override cancel' or 'remove cancel' with fentanyl 100 mcg/2ml fifteen times; surveillance video reportedly showed the employee blocking the camera's view, removing vials from a drawer and putting them in his pocket, and using a syringe and needle to take leftover waste from drip bags for personal use. Police said the employee later admitted to the theft of fentanyl waste, totaling about $430.
cases.status: Charged with larceny of controlled drugs

cases.title: A pharmacy technician diverted narcotics by taking and selling them, and the pharmacy's controlled-substance records were found inaccurate as a result
cases.method: A pharmacy technician took narcotics from the pharmacy and sold them; a subsequent state board order found the pharmacy had failed to maintain accurate records of the receipt and disposal of hydrocodone and alprazolam over an extended period.
cases.status: The technician was terminated and the technician's license was revoked by the state pharmacy board; the pharmacy itself was placed on two years' probation, fined $5,000, and assessed investigation costs by that board. A separate state board later granted the pharmacy's out-of-state permit application subject to one year of probation because of these violations.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician accused of removing pills from a filled Oxycontin prescription and returning it to conceal the theft
cases.method: Alleged to have pulled a customer's filled prescription from the staging area, removed pills, and returned the prescription to the staging area; the customer later reported 198 of 270 pills missing
cases.status: Registration summarily suspended pending a show cause hearing

cases.title: Applicant for reinstatement granted probation after prior controlled substance diversion from pharmacy
cases.method: diversion of a controlled substance from a pharmacy
cases.status: Reinstatement granted with 3 years probation

cases.title: Nurse at a medical center in Caliente investigated for unaccounted morphine; license revoked
cases.setting: a medical center in Caliente, Nevada
cases.method: investigated for two 2015 incidents involving unaccounted morphine; investigation indicated obtaining morphine syringes for patients but failing to document whether the drug was administered
cases.status: Nevada State Board of Nursing revoked the nursing license for five years for unprofessional conduct

cases.title: Pain clinic physician indicted for prescribing fentanyl, oxycodone and other controlled substances without patient examinations
cases.method: Charged by indictment with unlawful distribution of controlled substances: allegedly prescribing fentanyl, oxycodone, methadone, morphine and other controlled substances on many occasions without patients actually being seen by the physician, and billing Medicare, Medicaid and the Bureau of Workers' Compensation for medically unnecessary prescriptions; also alleged to have received payments from a pharmaceutical company for sham speaking engagements about a fentanyl spray.
cases.status: Federal grand jury indictment: 88 counts of unlawful distribution of a controlled substance, one count of unlawful distribution of a controlled substance with death resulting, eight counts of health care fraud and 17 counts of violating the anti-kickback law. Charges only; no finding or plea reported.

cases.title: Physician charged with health care fraud and distributing Suboxone without medical necessity through a clinic
cases.method: Charged in a federal indictment with a health care fraud scheme that involved marketing prescription creams in low-income neighborhoods and persistently mailing those creams to Medicaid customers, and with prescribing and distributing Suboxone without medical necessity.
cases.status: Charged in a seven-count federal indictment on October 30, 2018; scheduled for an initial appearance in federal court.

cases.title: Nurse practitioner forged physicians' signatures to issue unauthorized controlled-substance prescriptions at two Montgomery pill-mill practices
cases.setting: Family Practice and Mercy Family Health Care, Montgomery medical practices
cases.drug: fentanyl, hydrocodone, oxycodone, alprazolam, and methadone
cases.method: Convicted at trial of issuing unnecessary and illegitimate prescriptions for controlled substances and, because she lacked authority as a nurse practitioner to refill Schedule II prescriptions without physician approval, forging physicians' signatures on those prescriptions; the unnecessary office visits and unlawful prescriptions were billed to insurers. Conduct spanned 2013 through 2016, initially at a Montgomery medical practice and later at a second practice she opened.
cases.status: Convicted by federal jury on 17 counts of unlawful distribution of controlled substances, one count of conspiracy to distribute controlled substances, four counts of health care fraud, and one count of conspiracy to commit health care fraud; sentenced to 10 years and received enhancements for obstructing justice and abuse of trust.

cases.title: Physician found guilty of operating a pill mill and prescribing opioids without legitimate medical purpose
cases.method: prescribed opioids and other drugs without a legitimate medical purpose; operated a pill mill; aggravated trafficking in drugs; tampering with records; illegal processing of drug documents
cases.status: Found guilty on 187 counts; sentencing scheduled for July 3, 2019

cases.title: Anchorage nurse practitioner charged with manslaughter and drug distribution for opioid prescriptions without office visits
cases.drug: diazepam, oxycodone, tramadol, hydrocodone, and Ambien
cases.method: Alleged: used position as a nurse practitioner to fraudulently give a patient and others vast quantities of prescription opioids; routinely prescribed controlled substances to friends and acquaintances without office visits, chart notes, rationalization, or explanation, often via text or the internet; agreed to meet to write a prescription after a request for pain pills.
cases.status: Indicted on 18 felony counts including manslaughter and criminally negligent homicide plus drug distribution counts; pleaded not guilty; license suspended by the Alaska Board of Nursing. An outside review found no justification for many of the prescriptions; the nursing board had previously suspended the practitioner's license.

cases.title: Pain clinic physician pleaded guilty to operating a pill mill and selling oxycodone for kickbacks
cases.method: operated a pill mill out of his practice for more than seven years and sold oxycodone in exchange for financial kickbacks; also staged a break-in at his practice to make a fraudulent insurance claim
cases.status: pleaded guilty; sentenced to five years probation, ordered to pay a $5,000 fine, forfeit more than $524,000, and surrender his medical license and DEA registration

cases.title: Physician pleads guilty to illegally prescribing opioids and falsifying records at a Lake Milton medical office
cases.setting: a medical office in Lake Milton, Ohio
cases.drug: opioids including oxycodone and hydrocodone, often in combination with benzodiazepines and stimulants
cases.method: illegally prescribed controlled substances outside the usual course of professional practice and without a legitimate medical purpose; used false diagnoses, falsified patient pain intensity scales in medical charts, increased dosages, and prescribed for prolonged periods without evidence of efficacy; ignored urine drug screen results and warning signs of patient addiction and abuse; unlawfully prescribed opioids to two patients who later fatally overdosed and to an individual under the age of 21
cases.status: pleaded guilty to illegally distributing controlled substances, causing the deaths of two patients, unlawfully distributing a controlled substance to a person under the age of 21, and health care fraud; sentencing scheduled for May 17, 2022

cases.title: Mount Pleasant pharmacy technician charged with stealing OxyContin and Adderall from CVS pharmacy
cases.setting: CVS Pharmacy on Ben Sawyer Boulevard
cases.method: Allegedly stole tablets of OxyContin and Adderall from the pharmacy while working as a pharmacy technician.
cases.status: Charged with two counts of theft of a controlled substance; booked into the Al Cannon Detention Center and later released on own recognizance.

cases.title: Hospice nurse admitted diverting oxycodone and Oxycontin from two patients
cases.method: The nurse picked up prescriptions for two hospice patients, signed for oxycodone and Oxycontin, delivered fewer tablets than she signed for, and set up e-prescribing requests without physician orders; she admitted to police that she diverted prescription medication from the patients.
cases.status: The Board suspended the nurse's license for an indefinite period, stayed the suspension on compliance with treatment, monitoring, and practice restrictions, and restricted the nurse from working in settings with access to controlled substances.

cases.title: Pain clinic nurse practitioner convicted of diverting opioids to a family member using other patients' names
cases.setting: a pain management clinic (Eagle River Pain and Wellness)
cases.method: wrote opioid prescriptions in the names of other individuals in order to divert nearly 5,000 pills to a live-in, opioid-addicted partner, and created false appointment records for those individuals to conceal the diversion; also pre-signed and pre-dated prescriptions for non-medical staff to distribute to patients for cash when out of the office
cases.status: convicted by a federal jury on 10 felony counts, including distribution of a controlled substance resulting in death, distribution/dispensing of a controlled substance, and maintaining a drug-involved premises; per the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Alaska (Nov. 12, 2026), this jury conviction was later overturned because the presiding judge failed to recuse himself, and the defendant was resentenced after a guilty plea

cases.title: Pharmacy technician took controlled substance from pharmacy for personal use
cases.method: Took controlled substance from the pharmacy for personal use
cases.status: Suspended until cleared by a mental health professional plus 5 years rehabilitation probation

cases.title: Pharmacy technician admitted to theft of controlled substances from her employer; credential revoked
cases.method: admitted to the theft of various controlled substances from her employer
cases.status: credential revoked; prohibited from applying or reapplying to practice or assist in the practice of pharmacy

cases.title: Pain clinic nurse practitioner conspired to dispense fentanyl by forging a physician's signature on prescriptions
cases.method: Convicted of conspiring to prescribe fentanyl outside the usual course of professional practice and without a legitimate medical purpose; admitted to seeing patients without physician oversight while impaired by her own drug use, and to asking a co-defendant nurse practitioner to forge a physician's signature on controlled-substance prescriptions.
cases.status: Sentenced to 20 months in federal prison after a 50% sentence reduction for cooperating in the prosecution of the clinic's co-owning physicians.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician admitted to stealing controlled substances from employer pharmacy
cases.method: Admitted to the theft of controlled substances from the employer pharmacy.
cases.status: Credential revoked; prohibited from applying or reapplying to practice or assist in the practice of pharmacy.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician accused of forging controlled substance prescriptions from employer pharmacy
cases.method: Alleged to have forged controlled substance prescriptions from the employer pharmacy.
cases.status: Credential revoked; prohibited from applying or reapplying to practice or assist in the practice of pharmacy.

cases.title: Registrant's registration revoked for diversion of controlled substance from pharmacy
cases.method: diversion of a controlled substance from a pharmacy
cases.status: Revocation

cases.title: Nursing home director of nursing used pre-signed prescription pads to divert hydrocodone
cases.method: Used pre-signed prescription pads left by the facility's medical director to fax fraudulent prescriptions to the facility's pharmacy, then received and kept the narcotics from the pharmacy's courier instead of administering them
cases.status: Pleaded guilty to Theft of Property Second Degree; sentenced to 18 months in community corrections and surrendered nursing license

cases.title: National chain pharmacy manager disciplined after oxycodone reported lost/stolen as employee pilferage
cases.drug: Oxycodone HCL 10 mg and 15 mg tablets
cases.method: The pharmacy reported an occurrence classified as employee pilferage; a DEA report listed oxycodone HCL 10 mg and 15 mg tablets lost or stolen. The Board found the pharmacist violated patient safety and standard-of-care rules for filling questionable CII prescriptions without validation and for refusing-to-dispense requirements; fraud and false-record charges were dismissed as unsubstantiated.
cases.status: Consent order: license reprimanded, placed on probation for at least one year, required continuing education, and a $1,000 fine.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician's credential revoked for theft of controlled substances from employer pharmacy
cases.method: theft of controlled substances from employer pharmacy
cases.status: credential revoked; prohibited from applying or reapplying to practice or assist in the practice of pharmacy

cases.title: VA nurse pleaded guilty to stealing fentanyl, morphine and hydromorphone
cases.setting: Denver Veterans Affairs (VA) Medical Center, VA Eastern Colorado Health Care System
cases.method: stealing fentanyl, morphine and hydromorphone from the Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Denver
cases.status: Pleaded guilty; sentenced to 14 months in prison

cases.title: VA pharmacy supervisor suspected of stealing painkillers and testosterone over five years
cases.setting: George Wahlen Veterans Affairs (VA) Medical Center, VA Salt Lake City Health Care System
cases.method: suspected of stealing more than 24,000 painkillers and 25 vials of testosterone over five years
cases.status: Suspected; no disposition stated

cases.title: Arkansas nurse self-reported diverting and consuming hydrocodone from employer
cases.method: self-reported diverting and consuming hydrocodone from employer
cases.status: Self-reported; no disciplinary action stated

cases.title: Registered nurse sentenced to probation for stealing OxyContin from a hospital narcotics cabinet and replacing it with other medications
cases.method: Removed OxyContin from blister packs in a narcotics cabinet and replaced it with melatonin and acetaminophen, resealed the packs, and used the stolen OxyContin for personal use; pleaded guilty to obtaining a controlled substance by misrepresentation, fraud, forgery, deception, and subterfuge.
cases.status: Pleaded guilty on March 6, 2024; sentenced on May 24, 2024, to two years probation and a $100 special assessment; indicted by a federal grand jury in June 2023. Investigated by the FDA Office of Criminal Investigations and the DEA.

cases.title: Maui nurse sanctioned after alleged diversion of Adderall from patient medication packet
cases.setting: Nova Luna Inc., dba Nova Luna Center and 'Ai Pono Hawaii
cases.method: Allegedly diverted four Adderall tablets from a patient's medication pill packet, replaced them with four Seroquel tablets, and had no authorization to possess, obtain, furnish, or administer the Adderall herself.
cases.status: Board of Nursing sanctioned the nurse with a $5,000 fine on Aug. 1, 2024, in a board-approved settlement agreement. Also reported: Licensed nurse (charged under Hawaii nursing statute HRS 457 and nursing rules HAR 16-89).

cases.title: Former nurse accused of replacing fentanyl with tap water in IV drips at Oregon hospital
cases.method: accused of replacing prescribed fentanyl with nonsterile tap water in intravenous drips; police investigation into theft and misuse of controlled substances that resulted in patient infections; hospital officials believed an employee had been diverting fentanyl
cases.status: civil wrongful death and medical malpractice lawsuit filed against the hospital; the former nurse was arrested in June and charged with 44 counts of second-degree assault and has pleaded not guilty

cases.title: Pharmacist diverted phentermine and other prescription drugs using fictitious patient profiles at a Wicomico County pharmacy
cases.setting: a pharmacy in Wicomico County, Maryland
cases.drug: phentermine (Schedule IV CDS), cyclobenzaprine, tizanidine, and gabapentin
cases.method: Created a fictitious patient profile and used it to fill and purchase prescriptions for herself; recorded prescriptions as transmitted via telephone by a physician assistant; purchased with cash; used her driver's license to complete a purchase; diverted multiple prescription drugs and/or CDS.
cases.status: Consent Order: summary suspension lifted; license suspended effective April 8, 2025, for at least one year; $1,000 fine; substance use evaluation; possible rehabilitation contract; may petition to modify after six months and lift after one year; criminal case: agreement statement of facts to one count of obtaining a prescription drug by fraud, probation before judgment, one year unsupervised probation.

cases.title: VA hospital psychiatric nurse diverted amphetamine/dextroamphetamine and methylphenidate and tampered with patient medications
cases.setting: Veterans Administration Medical Center in White River Junction
cases.method: Diverted amphetamine/dextroamphetamine capsules from psychiatric patients, removed the regulated ingredients, and returned empty or nearly empty capsules to circulation; removed methylphenidate tablets and replaced them with hydroxyzine tablets for administration to patients; acquired amphetamine/dextroamphetamine and methylphenidate through fraud and deception.
cases.status: Pleaded guilty to two felony counts; sentencing planned for Oct. 23; plea agreement capped the proposed sentence at 24 months, with a maximum penalty of 14 years and $500,000; agreed to forfeit a New Hampshire nursing license.

cases.title: Registered nurse charged with unlawfully obtaining oxycodone, hydromorphone and fentanyl at a Horry County hospital
cases.method: Charged with theft of controlled substances after allegedly unlawfully obtaining quantities of oxycodone, hydromorphone and fentanyl on dates between Jan. 10 and April 11 while working as a registered nurse; also accused of furnishing false material or omitting material from an application, report or other required document, and the whereabouts of the medication could not be accounted for.
cases.status: Arrested and charged with three counts of theft of controlled substances and nine counts of violation of drug distribution law; released from J. Reuben Long Detention Center on a $12,000 bond. The South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation temporarily suspended the nurse's license on April 22, 2026; the hospital's parent company said the individual was no longer employed after an internal investigation.

cases.title: Pediatric intensive care nurse sentenced after guilty plea to obtaining morphine by fraud
cases.setting: University of Maryland Medical Center Pediatric Intensive Care Unit
cases.method: diverted morphine from a pediatric intensive care unit; documented an 8:30 a.m. intravenous morphine dose for a patient but did not document a later dose she told another nurse she had given; pleaded guilty to obtaining morphine by fraud
cases.status: Sentenced to 1 year, suspending all but 30 days, with two years of supervised probation; prohibited from caring for children during probation; excluded from state and federal healthcare programs. Pleaded guilty June 20, 2026; sentenced Sept. 9, 2026 in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City.

cases.title: Registered nurse diverted a Schedule II controlled substance from the workplace
cases.method: diverted a Schedule II controlled substance from the workplace
cases.status: amended memorandum of agreement; relocated to Nebraska

cases.title: Nurse practitioner self-administered controlled substances taken from office stock
cases.method: took controlled substances from her office stock without a prescription and self-administered them
cases.status: consent agreement with five years probation, drug rehabilitation counseling, psychiatric/psychological therapy, random testing, and restrictions on controlled-substance access and practice

cases.title: Pharmacy licensee in Mitchell, SD diverted prescription drugs for personal use and received three-year probation
cases.method: Diverted prescription drugs for personal use; violated laws and rules governing pharmacy practice.
cases.status: Three-year probation effective September 29, 2014; required continued participation in a monitored program for health professionals, quarterly reports to the Board, and passage of the Multistate Pharmacy Jurisprudence Exam before completing probation.

cases.title: Rawlins physician charged with prescribing oxycodone and other controlled substances outside legitimate medical practice
cases.drug: oxycodone, alprazolam, tramadol, promethazine with codeine, amphetamine/dextroamphetamine, hydrocodone
cases.method: Charged in a 32-count federal indictment with dispensing controlled substances from 2014 to 2017 often without a legitimate medical purpose and outside the usual course of professional practice, including to persons under 21 and to pregnant women under 21; the state medical board found in 2017 that the physician was inappropriately prescribing controlled substances for other than legitimate purposes, prescribing to known abusers, and offering drugs in exchange for sex.
cases.status: Federal criminal charges (32 counts) with a guilty plea scheduled; 2017 license suspension; voluntary relinquishment of license accepted August 2018.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician's credential revoked for theft of oxycodone tablets from a patient's prescription
cases.method: theft of eight oxycodone tablets from a patient's prescription
cases.status: credential revoked; prohibited from applying or reapplying to practice or assist in the practice of pharmacy

cases.title: Admission of taking controlled substances from a pharmacy for personal use
cases.method: Admitted to taking drugs without authorization from the pharmacy for personal use (2 counts)
cases.status: 90 days suspension + 5 year probation

cases.title: Default order for diversion of controlled substance from pharmacy
cases.method: Diversion of controlled substance from pharmacy
cases.status: Revocation

cases.title: Pharmacist admitted to taking controlled substances without authorization from the pharmacy for personal use
cases.method: Admitted to taking controlled substances without authorization from the pharmacy for personal use (2 counts); felony theft of a controlled substance (deferred).
cases.status: 120 day suspension + 5 year rehabilitation probation

cases.title: Pharmacist at Fairview Pharmacy Consultants obtained and consumed controlled substances without authorization
cases.method: obtaining and consuming controlled substances without authorization
cases.status: license suspended indefinitely, stayed for five years with conditions

cases.title: Psychiatrist in Salisbury, MD, reprimanded for writing controlled dangerous substance prescriptions for himself under others' names
cases.method: wrote prescriptions for controlled dangerous substances for himself in the names of others and issued undated CDS for patients
cases.status: Reprimand; terms and conditions for four years

cases.title: Physician assistant applicant found guilty by court-martial of self-prescribing controlled substances and prescribing them for his spouse without authorization
cases.method: found guilty by Navy court-martial of self-prescribing and prescribing for his spouse controlled dangerous substances without authorization
cases.status: Application for certification denied

cases.title: Registered nurse diverted morphine and fentanyl from Children's Hospital of Wisconsin stock or waste
cases.method: The Board found that the nurse diverted morphine and fentanyl from hospital stock or waste for personal use over four years until June 28, 2004, and consumed the substances at work without a prescription or other authority. The nurse was also criminally charged with unlawfully obtaining a controlled substance.
cases.status: License suspended for six months, then indefinitely, with conditions including treatment, monitoring, and restricted access to controlled substances; partial costs of $200.

cases.title: Physician removed hospital supplies to administer a controlled substance to a friend and falsified test records to conceal it
cases.method: Removed supplies from a hospital to intravenously administer a controlled dangerous substance to an addicted friend, then arranged for the friend's blood to be tested with results filed under another inpatient's name to conceal the act.
cases.status: License revocation

cases.title: Psychiatrist summarily suspended for prescribing controlled substances in others' names and picking up prescriptions
cases.method: prescribing large quantities of CDS in the names of 12 individuals for whom the physician could not provide medical records, and picking up the filled prescriptions himself
cases.status: Summary Suspension

cases.title: Pathologist suspended for narcotic/CDS abuse and illegal prescribing
cases.method: being addicted to or habitually abusing any narcotic or CDS; willfully making or filing a false report in the practice of medicine and when making application for licensure; and prescribing drugs for illegal or illegitimate medical purposes
cases.status: Suspension for 5 years with terms and conditions; should the suspension be stayed, probation for 5 years with terms and conditions

cases.title: Internist's reinstatement denied over past substance abuse and fraud in obtaining controlled dangerous substances
cases.method: past misconduct concerning substance abuse and fraud in obtaining controlled dangerous substances and submitting false statements when he obtained licensure in Maryland
cases.status: Reinstatement Denied; the Board will not accept any further applications for reinstatement for 5 years

cases.title: General practice physician summarily suspended after admitting cocaine use in violation of probation
cases.method: Tested positive for cocaine in violation of a prior consent order and admitted to using cocaine on the occasion that produced the positive test.
cases.status: Summary suspension

cases.title: Hospital anesthesiologist diverted controlled dangerous substances from medication management system and falsified patient records
cases.method: diverted controlled dangerous substances from a hospital medication management system and placed false information in patient medical records to conceal the diversion
cases.status: Summary Suspension

cases.title: Unlicensed resident removed narcotic patches from nursing home patient
cases.method: unlawfully removed narcotic-eluding patches from a ventilator-dependent patient at a nursing home. He posed as a licensed physician and entered the nursing home's premises on several occasions before the patches were removed.
cases.status: Permanent Revocation; any application for licensure, registration, or certification will not be accepted

cases.title: General practice physician accused of self-administering narcotics and writing prescriptions to family and staff without medical records
cases.method: Board investigative findings alleged the physician was addicted to CDS, overdosed on narcotics in December 2008, and wrote multiple prescriptions to family members and office staff without maintaining medical records, while allowing patients to keep their own medical records.
cases.status: Summary suspension

cases.title: Anesthesiologist diverted controlled substances from his workplace for personal use
cases.method: Diverted CDS from his workplace for his personal use amid substance abuse issues
cases.status: Reprimand; suspension until the physician's license is activated by the Oregon Medical Board

cases.title: Diagnostic radiologist prescribed controlled substances in the names of others for his own use
cases.method: The Board found that the physician prescribed CDS and other prescription medications in the names of other people for his own personal use.
cases.status: Suspension for a minimum of 6 months, immediately stayed; Probation for a minimum of 5 years subject to terms and conditions.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician admitted diverting Valium, Promethazine/Codeine Syrup, Vicodin, Loratadine, and Soma from Pharmacy A
cases.drug: Valium, Promethazine/Codeine Syrup, Vicodin, Loratadine, and Soma
cases.method: Admitted diverting drugs from Pharmacy A from the fall of 2010 until the spring of 2011; obtained the drugs for a family member and a friend, not for personal use.
cases.status: Summarily suspended on January 31, 2012; permanently surrendered registration to practice as a pharmacy technician, with the Board accepting the surrender as a final order.

cases.title: Psychiatrist found to have unlawfully possessed controlled substances taken back from patients and kept no required records
cases.drug: controlled substances including fentanyl patches, oxycodone, OxyContin, methadone, Suboxone, hydrocodone, benzodiazepines, and Lyrica samples
cases.method: Took back and retained already-dispensed controlled substances directly from patients outside the CSA's closed distribution system, and failed to maintain any inventory or records of the controlled substances he received or the drug samples kept in his office; a separate allegation that he redistributed these drugs to other patients was investigated but found unproven.
cases.status: DEA registration renewal granted subject to a six-month suspension and restriction to non-narcotic controlled substances only; DATA-Waiver authority to prescribe Suboxone/Subutex revoked.

cases.title: Roseville Pharmacy break-ins lead to indictment for theft of Schedule II and III controlled substances
cases.drug: Schedule II and Schedule III controlled substances
cases.method: alleged break-ins and theft of 6,140 Schedule II and Schedule III controlled substances from a pharmacy
cases.status: indicted on 69 felony counts: 4 counts of breaking and entering, 35 counts of theft of drugs and 30 counts of possession of dangerous drugs

cases.title: Emergency room nurse sentenced for stealing prescription drugs from patient accounts via a hospital dispensing system
cases.method: Used their own name to access a computerized dispensing system at the hospital and withdrew drugs in the names of emergency room patients; also falsified private records.
cases.status: Pleaded guilty to 10 counts of stealing drugs and three counts of falsifying private records; sentenced to two years in prison with all but six months suspended, a consecutive two-year term all suspended, four years of probation, $4,000 in fines and $8,318 in restitution, and prohibited from employment giving access to controlled substances; nursing license under suspension.

cases.title: UW Hospital nurse charged in morphine and hydromorphone syringe diversion
cases.method: Admitted to hospital staff that she was diverting pain-management drugs and taking them for herself since October 2013; a police investigation found she accessed morphine syringes from a secured machine, replaced them with syringes containing water or an unknown liquid, and took the morphine syringes for herself in at least 42 instances.
cases.status: Arrested on June 12 and was to be charged with 42 felony counts of diversion of drugs and 42 counts of reckless injury; no longer employed by UW Hospital.

cases.title: Physician indicted for trafficking controlled substances prescribed to friends and co-workers
cases.method: The physician was alleged to have prescribed controlled substances to friends and co-workers who were not patients and not for a legitimate medical purpose, leading to an indictment on 26 felony counts of trafficking in drugs.
cases.status: Indicted on 26 felony counts of trafficking in drugs; pleaded not guilty and was released on a $10,000 personal recognizance bond.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician admitted taking Xanax, Lortab and Luminal without payment from a national chain pharmacy
cases.setting: a national chain pharmacy in Baltimore, Maryland
cases.drug: Xanax (alprazolam) 2 mg, Lortab (hydrocodone-APAP) 10/500 mg, Luminal (phenobarbital) 60 mg and 16.2 mg
cases.method: admitted orally and in writing to taking the drugs without payment and stated the count was not accurate and that she stole the drugs
cases.status: registration summarily suspended by the State Board of Pharmacy; terminated from employment; criminally charged in the District Court of Maryland for Baltimore County with theft less than $1,000 and theft-scheme less than $1,000

cases.title: Search warrant at Norwalk, OH physician's office over alleged prescriptions issued while physician absent
cases.setting: a physician's office in Norwalk, OH
cases.method: Alleged issuance of prescriptions for controlled and non-controlled substances while the physician was absent from the office due to illness; prescriptions were not dated as of the day issued.
cases.status: Search warrant served; evidence seized; no arrests; case to be presented to the Huron County Prosecutor's Office for requested charges of Illegal Processing of Drug Documents and Trafficking in Drugs.

cases.title: Hospital nurse diverted fentanyl from secure medication management stations
cases.method: The hospital investigation concluded the nurse diverted 18 vials of fentanyl between May 2 and 3, 2015, by accessing a secure medication management station on a day off, making duplicate withdrawals for the same patient from multiple stations, withdrawing medication while not scheduled to work, and withdrawing from units where not actively providing patient care. The nurse neither admitted nor denied the allegations.
cases.status: Professional nursing license suspended for an indefinite period; suspension may be stayed after three months under conditions, including drug and alcohol treatment, monitoring, and practice limitations.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician diverted over 216,000 Norco tablets from a retail pharmacy while the pharmacist-in-charge failed to detect the theft
cases.method: A pharmacy technician diverted the drug over a roughly two-year period by repeatedly ordering large quantities to be delivered on days she worked, intercepting and hiding the bottles in the storeroom, destroying the packing invoices, and removing the drugs to her car while the on-duty pharmacist was on break. The pharmacist-in-charge failed to review delivery invoices, restrict access to the phone-ordering passcode, or conduct random audits that could have detected the diversion sooner.
cases.status: The California State Board of Pharmacy found grounds for discipline after a hearing and revoked the pharmacist-in-charge's license but stayed the revocation, placing the license on three years' probation with conditions; a petition for writ of administrative mandate challenging the discipline was denied, and the Court of Appeal affirmed.

cases.title: Cleveland-area diet clinic pill mill indicted for trafficking phentermine and scheduled stimulants
cases.setting: Diet Med Clinics in Mayfield Heights, Fairview Park, and Mentor
cases.method: indicted for running a pill mill that illegally sold more than a million doses of weight loss medication; a physician allegedly used credentials to purchase large quantities of scheduled stimulants while having little or no patient contact as hundreds of thousands of doses were dispensed directly from the clinics
cases.status: charged in a 227-count indictment with Engaging in a Pattern of Corrupt Activity, Drug Trafficking, and Money Laundering; arraignment scheduled for September 1

cases.title: Nurse accused of diverting fentanyl and hydromorphone at Danville hospital
cases.method: Was accused of diverting and tampering with vials of fentanyl and injectable hydromorphone intended for patients; hospital discovered that tops of several vials had been removed or tampered with, including 14 of 20 fentanyl vials whose tops popped off and one vial with a dry white film appearing to be superglue.
cases.status: Was already serving a three-year prison sentence for tampering with consumer products at Sovah Health-Danville.

cases.title: Walgreens pharmacy technician diverted Norco 10 and Norco 7.5
cases.method: admitted to taking Norco 10 and Norco 7.5 from the Walgreens pharmacy where she worked
cases.status: The board accepted the voluntary surrender of the pharmacy technician registration, revoked it, and imposed $250 in investigation costs.

cases.title: Walgreens pharmacist diverted Adderall and Allegra D
cases.method: admitted to taking Adderall and Allegra D from the Walgreens pharmacy where she worked
cases.status: The board accepted the voluntary surrender of the pharmacist license, revoked it, and imposed $750 in investigation costs.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician diverted OxyContin from AccuDose machines at Baptist Medical Center
cases.method: admitted to taking OxyContin from the AccuDose machines at Baptist Medical Center
cases.status: The board accepted the voluntary surrender of the pharmacy technician registration, revoked it, and imposed $250 in investigation costs.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician diverted Norco, Percocet, and MS Contin from Magee General Hospital pharmacy
cases.method: admitted to taking Norco, Percocet and MS Contin from the pharmacy at Magee General Hospital where she worked
cases.status: The board accepted the voluntary surrender of the pharmacy technician registration, revoked it, and imposed $350 in investigation costs.

cases.title: Registered pharmacy technician took controlled substances from a pharmacy for purposes of sale
cases.method: took controlled substances from the pharmacy for purposes of sale
cases.status: 30-day suspension and 5 years probation

cases.title: Registered pharmacy technician took controlled substances from a pharmacy for use by a family member
cases.method: took controlled substances from the pharmacy for use by a family member
cases.status: revocation

cases.title: Pharmacy technician surrendered registration after admitted theft of controlled substances from Walgreens pharmacy
cases.method: Admitted to theft of controlled substances from the Walgreens pharmacy where the technician worked.
cases.status: Voluntary surrender of pharmacy technician registration accepted; registration revoked; ordered to pay $150.00 in investigation costs.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician surrendered registration after admitting to ingesting THC-infused chocolate while working at Kroger pharmacy
cases.method: Admitted to ingestion of chocolate infused with THC while working at Kroger Pharmacy #493.
cases.status: Voluntary surrender of pharmacy technician registration accepted; registration revoked; may petition for reinstatement after at least one year.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician took controlled substances from a pharmacy
cases.method: Took controlled substances from the pharmacy.
cases.status: Revocation

cases.title: Pharmacy technician reinstated after taking a controlled substance from a pharmacy for personal use
cases.method: Took a controlled substance from the pharmacy for personal use (dated 06/06/2019), cited in connection with a prior board order
cases.status: Granted reinstatement with 3 years probation

cases.title: Hospital nurse anesthetist accused of diverting fentanyl and propofol intended for surgical patients
cases.method: Accused of diverting fentanyl and propofol intended for patients' surgical pain control for his own use, and of going to extreme lengths to avoid drug testing after colleagues raised concerns.
cases.status: Board of Nursing settlement reported to include two years of probation, quarterly supervisor reports, and random drug testing; an earlier proposed settlement had included 28 days of rehab, five years of probation, and more frequent drug testing.

cases.title: Pharmacy technician charged with taking Promethazine-Codeine syrup from pharmacy
cases.method: Allegedly seen taking two bottles of Promethazine-Codeine Syrup from the pharmacy in December 2023; approximately 46 bottles of Promethazine-Codeine were unaccounted for during times the technician worked at pharmacies from January to December 2022.
cases.status: Charged with unprofessional conduct by the Pharmacy Quality Assurance Commission in May 2024.

cases.title: Clinic pharmacy assistant charged with stealing OxyContin and Oxycodone prescriptions from the clinic where she worked
cases.method: Charges state that in November 2023 the pharmacy assistant stole prescriptions for OxyContin and Oxycodone from the clinic where she worked.
cases.status: Charged with unprofessional conduct by the Pharmacy Quality Assurance Commission in May 2024; the case is pending.

cases.title: ICU nurse accused of diverting patients' liquid fentanyl and replacing it with tap water at a Medford, Oregon hospital
cases.method: Allegedly diverted patients' liquid fentanyl for personal use and replaced it with nonsterile tap water, which was linked to central line infections; police said the charges reflect the number of patients affected.
cases.status: Arrested and charged with 44 counts of second-degree assault; the nurse had voluntarily agreed in November 2023 to a nursing license suspension pending completion of an investigation and had left the hospital in July 2023. Indicted by a Jackson County grand jury on the 44 second-degree assault counts; trial was set for September 2026.
